claim.statement: A previously authorized effect must not execute after the governing authority state changes. At execution, the permit must still match the current authority revision and exact effect; stale, expired, replayed, or retargeted permits fail closed before the local effect is invoked. A successful local effect produces a receipt bound to the permit, effect digest, authority revision, and outcome.
claim.boundedness: This claim is limited to the in-memory local reference boundary and local governed consequence path. It does not claim production hardening, enterprise high availability, external-system enforcement, certification, or universal deployment security.

sequence: authorize exact effect under authority revision N
change or revoke authority so current revision becomes N+1
attempt execution using the permit issued at revision N

external_target.title: Runtime Execution Boundary
external_target.review_scope: The boundary that governs whether consequential execution may begin and enforces the Admissibility Determination at activation.

reciprocal_challenge.primary_question: What happens when authority or another governing condition changes after an earlier admissibility or authorization decision but before the consequential effect occurs?

shared_timeline.event: The proposed consequence is admissible or authorized under the then-current governing state.
Authority or another governing condition materially changes or is revoked.
The consequential effect is attempted using the earlier decision or authorization.

reciprocal_challenge.heimel_required_result: The stale authorization cannot produce the effect. Current governing state must be satisfied at consequence time, otherwise execution fails closed before effect.
reciprocal_challenge.question_for_reb01: Does REB-01 v1.0 independently detect or require re-evaluation of the T1 change before T2 effect activation, or can a previously valid Admissibility Determination remain operative across that change?
reciprocal_challenge.comparison_rule: Compare responsibility allocation and observable behavior, not terminology or architectural branding.

kill_conditions: The reviewed artifact or version is not immutable or cannot be uniquely identified.
The review requires changing either architecture before its current behavior can be evaluated.
The proposed test cannot distinguish a stale-authority effect from a fresh-authority effect.
Required execution or evidence artifacts cannot be independently inspected or replayed within the agreed boundary.
A party must disclose excluded private material for the bounded claim to be evaluated.
required_review_evidence: negative case showing stale authority cannot cause effect
evidence showing whether the effect occurred
replay or equivalent independent verification artifact

severity.critical: A stale or revoked authority state can still produce the consequential effect through the reviewed boundary.
severity.high: The boundary rejects the effect but cannot produce sufficient evidence to bind the rejection or effect attempt to the governing state and proposed consequence.
severity.medium: The required behavior exists but the version, protocol, or evidence binding is ambiguous enough to prevent independent replay.
severity.low: Non-semantic ambiguity or documentation defect that does not alter the bounded outcome.

remediation_rule: Findings are reported against the frozen reviewed artifact. Remediation, if any, occurs separately and does not rewrite the original review result.
exclusions: RiCo-01 is not reopened or modified by this review.
The review does not claim equivalence between ManChine and Heimel architectures.
The review does not evaluate model quality, reasoning quality, policy quality, or general AI safety.
The review does not expand the Heimel claim beyond the cited local reference implementation and evidence surface.
Protocol review and execution are separate gates; completion of this manifest does not authorize execution.
